dora128adj_avp_8ep.kim_feedback: 2026-09-17: "Even looking at the spectra of the worst offenders, I'm not sure now how I would automate. The only thing I see is that they have lots of wide peaks and valleys and they're thin" -- e.g. dora128adj_avp_8ep_ptm ep6 gf_05 (mixtape idx 43): ~5dB peak 5.5-7.5k, ~3dB peak 10-12k (may be hi-hats but stands out), valley at 236Hz (near the track's own B3 center); ep3 gf_08 (idx 39): 5.3-7.5k and 10.5-14k bumps, dip at 211Hz; ep3 gf_09 (idx 22): 8dB bump 1.5-4.5k on a distorted-guitar-like lead, midrange crunch worsened by SA3's gritty HF hallucination; ep6 gf_00 (idx 19): uneven contour, "nasal grating"; ep3 gf_13 (idx 17): "very in-your-face cheesegrater timbre." "Altogether the averaged 65k size spectrum of the track is like a roller coaster... A bigger issue into the sound is that most of these tracks are very distorted. Not like digitally clipped, but like they are fed through a smooth distortion, really pushing the levels... maybe growing weights blow some values over... there's a pretty evident pattern there... the model seems to create harsh timbres... I don't think it's worth our time to try to fix this, I want to have a mix to share with some people." Possible (UNCONFIRMED) mechanism: latent-scale runaway from growing weights, same family as DISCOVERIES.md 2026-08-10 full-FT latent-scale runaway -> spectral drone (z0 std 5.6 vs healthy 1.134) -- not verified for this DoRA arm specifically. GHOST-NOTE attempted an rms_energy_air LatCH-guided damping fix first (eval/hf_latch_bracket.py, two bracket rounds) -- found NULL/no-op regardless of gain or start_pct, root-caused to a real bug: _latch_guided_generate always calls the euler-sampler guided path, silently ignoring this model's true rf_denoiser/ping-pong sampler (see commit 8e65acd, "latch: guidance must not silently swap the model's native sampler"). Per Kim's direction, this is NOT being pursued further -- 5 worst clips quarantined, mixtape rebuilt without them.

fp32cmp_avp_t4096_bs1_lr1e4.recipe_legacy_str: LUMI precision/context campaign: DoRA-rows r128 α128 (s=1), fp32 (32-true) training, T=4096 latent-frame crops (380.4s), batch 1, lr 1e-4, medium-base, 8 epochs, FusionOpt. Full-context arm — the T-regime flagship.
fp32cmp_avp_t4096_bs1_lr1e4.one_liner: fp32-vs-bf16 precision A/B: fp32 attention, DoRA-r128 FusionOpt, avp, T4096 (380.4s), bs1, lr1e-4.
fp32cmp_avp_t4096_bs1_lr1e4.why: Precision A/B on RDNA4: does fp32 attention (vs bf16 throughout) actually improve quality, and is the improvement worth the ~compute cost? Kim's preliminary listening verdict (2026-07-20, recorded in run_meta kim_feedback + WORKLOG): fp32 beats bf16 by ear in most ways (better sound separation, less noisy high end), worse in very few (occasional less punch, likely source-faithfulness not a defect) -- not a comprehensive audit. Two questions flagged as undecided then: bs1-vs-bs4, and whether the fp32 edge holds at longer training context (fixed-20s eval grids can't show trained-context effects) -- the second question is what the fp32frames family (T512-T4096, fp32 only) actually answers, since fp32cmp itself only has T512+T4096, no T2048.

compare_against.axis: precision (fp32 attention vs bf16 throughout) -- the matched corpus/bs/lr sibling, the primary A/B
training context length (T512/1024/2048/4096) at fp32 -- does the precision edge hold as context grows

fp32cmp_avp_t4096_bs1_lr1e4.verdict: Kim's preliminary ear verdict (fp32 > bf16 in most ways) stands, not comprehensively audited. fullft_goa_t256.why: LUMI FULL fine-tune campaign (Kim direct, 2026-07-17/20): the entire 1.4B-parameter DiT is fine-tuned (not a low-rank adapter) on goa-only crops at T=256 latent frames, bf16, FusionOpt optimizer at lr 1e-4 for 8 epochs. fullft_goa_t256.verdict: Kim's 2026-07-23 policy verdict covers this family: full fine-tunes rated above adapter-only by ear, period (the ruling bundles 'fp32 + fullft'; note this campaign trained bf16 — the precision half of that ruling comes from the fp32cmp sibling campaign). Two structural caveats: (1) 8-epoch-era terminal — Kim's same ruling made 15 epochs the new default ('ep7 is often the first really good one'), so this ep7 checkpoint stops at the threshold of good; the winning-arms +40ep continuation exists because of exactly this. (2) NO low-rank distillation path: the delta is near-full-rank — r128 SVD extraction keeps only ~25.7% of its energy, and that fraction is INVARIANT across all 10 parents (±0.2pp over both corpora and T256-T4096; the rank structure is training-regime-determined, not data-determined) — so this model ships/continues as full weights or not at all. Per-T quality trend within THIS family is not separately measured; the fp32frames sibling family (different precision/optimizer) shows T4096>=T2048 production quality at native lengths — indicative only. Corpus rule: goa-trained weights are never published (commercial-music tier 2) — internal research artifact.

fullft_avp_t4096.verdict: Kim's 2026-07-23 policy verdict covers this family: full fine-tunes rated above adapter-only by ear, period (the ruling bundles 'fp32 + fullft'; note this campaign trained bf16 — the precision half of that ruling comes from the fp32cmp sibling campaign). Two structural caveats: (1) 8-epoch-era terminal — Kim's same ruling made 15 epochs the new default ('ep7 is often the first really good one'), so this ep7 checkpoint stops at the threshold of good; the winning-arms +40ep continuation exists because of exactly this. (2) NO low-rank distillation path: the delta is near-full-rank — r128 SVD extraction keeps only ~25.7% of its energy, and that fraction is INVARIANT across all 10 parents (±0.2pp over both corpora and T256-T4096; the rank structure is training-regime-determined, not data-determined) — so this model ships/continues as full weights or not at all. Per-T quality trend within THIS family is not separately measured; the fp32frames sibling family (different precision/optimizer) shows T4096>=T2048 production quality at native lengths — indicative only. Corpus: Kim's own avp material — publishable-lineage candidate once the CC dataset path lands, still internal for now.

fp32cmp_goa_t4096_bs4_lr1e4_ptm.recipe: SAME adapter file as fp32cmp_goa_t4096_bs4_lr1e4 (DoRA-rows r128 α128, fp32, T=4096, bs4, lr 1e-4, trained on medium-BASE) -- here applied to the POST-TRAINED medium (rf_denoiser / ping-pong sampler) at its native config: steps 8, cfg 1. Tests the Discord/Dadabots claim (+ Zach@Stability's layer argument: adapters concentrate in the middle 'knowledge' layers, ARC post-training rewrites the last decoder layers, so they compose) that base-trained L/DoRAs transfer to the post-trained model. Compare against the medium-base rows of the same label.

fp32cmp_goa_t4096_bs4_lr1e4_ptm.why: Precision A/B on RDNA4: does fp32 attention (vs bf16 throughout) actually improve quality, and is the improvement worth the ~compute cost? Kim's preliminary listening verdict (2026-07-20, recorded in run_meta kim_feedback + WORKLOG): fp32 beats bf16 by ear in most ways (better sound separation, less noisy high end), worse in very few (occasional less punch, likely source-faithfulness not a defect) -- not a comprehensive audit. Two questions flagged as undecided then: bs1-vs-bs4, and whether the fp32 edge holds at longer training context (fixed-20s eval grids can't show trained-context effects) -- the second question is what the fp32frames family (T512-T4096, fp32 only) actually answers, since fp32cmp itself only has T512+T4096, no T2048.

adamw_avp_t512_bs1_lr1e4.one_liner: AdamW-vs-FusionOpt A/B: DoRA-r128 on avp, bf16, lr 1e-4, batch 1, T512 (47.6s).
adamw_avp_t512_bs1_lr1e4.why: AdamW and FusionOpt were found to land in nearly-orthogonal weight-space basins (dir cos ~0.1, Fusion moves ~2x farther for the same steps -- CONTINUITY's weight-space read, WORKLOG 2026-07-24) -- so the weight delta alone proves the optimizers are DIFFERENT, not which is BETTER. This sweep answers that with metrics: same DoRA-rows r128 arch/rank/target-modules/corpus as the fp32frames family, only the optimizer (AdamW vs FusionOpt) and precision (bf16 vs fp32) differ, so any metric gap traces to the optimizer/precision choice, not a confound.

xftlora16_fullft_avp_t1024.note: auto: recipe extracted from checkpoint; evaluation sentence pending
xftlora16_fullft_avp_t1024.one_liner: SVD-extracted LoRA r16 from the avp t1024 whole-DiT fullft (fullft_avp_t1024) — task-#71 distillation test. Finding: the fullft delta is near-full-rank, so r16 recovers only ~4.5% of its energy (measured across all 10 fullft parents — invariant ±0.2pp); kept as A/B evidence, NOT a shippable model.
xftlora16_fullft_avp_t1024.why: Kim's hypothesis (task #71, 2026-07-23/24): a full-DiT fine-tune (fullft) is empirically 'just better' than a matched-rank trained adapter — can that quality be shipped cheaply by SVD-truncating the weight delta (deltaW = W_fullft − W_base) down to a small adapter? Tested by extracting LoRA/DoRA adapters at ranks {16,64,128} from each of 10 fullft arms (avp/goa × t256/512/1024/2048/4096) via truncated SVD (Eckart-Young best rank-r approximation of deltaW), then auditioning and measuring the singular-value energy spectrum of the delta itself. The DoRA variant additionally stores magnitude = row_norm(W_fullft). This member is the LoRA r16 extraction from fullft_avp_t1024.
xftlora16_fullft_avp_t1024.verdict: NO — a full fine-tune does NOT distill to a small adapter: the weight-delta is near-full-rank, not low-rank like a style LoRA's. Uniform-rank energy captured (extracted ranks measured across ALL 10 fullft parents — INVARIANT ±0.2pp across both corpora and every context length T256–T4096; higher-rank spectrum shape from the goa_t256 reference): 4.5% @r16, 14.8% @r64, 25.7% @r128, and it takes r512/r1024 for 65%/89.5%. Per-module median rank for 90% energy runs 49–72% of the 1536 hidden dim — nothing 'small'. The invariance is itself a finding: the delta's spectral shape is TRAINING-REGIME-determined (same optimizer/lr/epochs → same spectrum), not data-determined — the rank-side sibling of the ‖dW‖∝LR magnitude law. ~57 of the 60 extracted adapters are glitch/noise at these ranks and were never shipped; a 3-pair matched-rank A/B (r16/r128, avp+goa) on xft_distillation.html makes the contrast audible. A finding, not a shippable model family (credit: task #71 GHOST-NOTE extraction + CONTINUITY SV-spectrum reframe + per-arm invariance sweep, task #77).

xftdora128_fullft_goa_t512.one_liner: SVD-extracted DoRA r128 from the goa t512 whole-DiT fullft (fullft_goa_t512) — task-#71 distillation test. Finding: the fullft delta is near-full-rank, so r128 recovers only ~25.7% of its energy (measured across all 10 fullft parents — invariant ±0.2pp); kept as A/B evidence, NOT a shippable model.
xftdora128_fullft_goa_t512.why: Kim's hypothesis (task #71, 2026-07-23/24): a full-DiT fine-tune (fullft) is empirically 'just better' than a matched-rank trained adapter — can that quality be shipped cheaply by SVD-truncating the weight delta (deltaW = W_fullft − W_base) down to a small adapter? Tested by extracting LoRA/DoRA adapters at ranks {16,64,128} from each of 10 fullft arms (avp/goa × t256/512/1024/2048/4096) via truncated SVD (Eckart-Young best rank-r approximation of deltaW), then auditioning and measuring the singular-value energy spectrum of the delta itself. The DoRA variant additionally stores magnitude = row_norm(W_fullft). This member is the DoRA r128 extraction from fullft_goa_t512.
xftdora128_fullft_goa_t512.verdict: NO — a full fine-tune does NOT distill to a small adapter: the weight-delta is near-full-rank, not low-rank like a style LoRA's. Uniform-rank energy captured (extracted ranks measured across ALL 10 fullft parents — INVARIANT ±0.2pp across both corpora and every context length T256–T4096; higher-rank spectrum shape from the goa_t256 reference): 4.5% @r16, 14.8% @r64, 25.7% @r128, and it takes r512/r1024 for 65%/89.5%. Per-module median rank for 90% energy runs 49–72% of the 1536 hidden dim — nothing 'small'. The invariance is itself a finding: the delta's spectral shape is TRAINING-REGIME-determined (same optimizer/lr/epochs → same spectrum), not data-determined — the rank-side sibling of the ‖dW‖∝LR magnitude law. ~57 of the 60 extracted adapters are glitch/noise at these ranks and were never shipped; a 3-pair matched-rank A/B (r16/r128, avp+goa) on xft_distillation.html makes the contrast audible. A finding, not a shippable model family (credit: task #71 GHOST-NOTE extraction + CONTINUITY SV-spectrum reframe + per-arm invariance sweep, task #77).

headb_base_s1.purpose: B9, Kim direct 2026-08-21: "take our best full finetune, and train our FiLM, melody and LATCH heads with best known values and Fusion on top of that instead of the base model." 8 single-GCD arms: r0 Head-B FiLM (melody_contour) on the FULL-FT backbone — the backbone-dependent piece — against r1, the same head on medium-base as a matched same-seed control; r2-r7 are latent readout heads (f0_other, f0_bass, hpcp, rms_energy_bass, onset_envelope, spectral_flatness) retrained with the best known recipe: Fusion SF-NorMuon + adaln_zero + EMA 0.999 + cosine fusion-decay (undamped NS5 is the drone mechanism) + val split BY SOURCE TRACK (crop-split leaks sibling crops).

lreq_goa_lr1e4.purpose: The R2(t)-gate mode A/B + seed pairs (CONTINUITY 2026-08-06, burn-day 2026-08-21). Identical to the subspace-loss grid EXCEPT the basis: melody_subspace15_selective_v3 instead of v2. Motivated by the melody machinery-audit — the v2 basis (top-15 melody VARIANCE) had ~ZERO melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x), so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody, the probable reason #59 came back weak. v3 (whitened CSP) is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. K in {2,5,12}, matched to the v2 grid so arms compare directly. || The original SUBSPACE-WEIGHTED RF LOSS grid (CONTINUITY 2026-07-30, Kim direct). Counter to diffusion spectral bias (tau ~ 1/lambda, arXiv 2503.03206): melody is a measured 15-dim latent subspace holding only 9.3% of corpus variance, so plain RF gradient-starves it. Upweights the RF error's melody-subspace component by K (loss = mse + (K-1)*subspace_share; K=1 is byte-identical to off). K in {2,5,12}. Recipe = lreq_goa_lr1e4 EXACTLY, so the lr-equiv middle arm IS the K=1 baseline and no extra baseline burn was needed. ⚠ This grid used the v2 (melody-VARIANCE) basis later shown to have ~zero held-out selectivity — see subloss_tgate_modes for the v3 replacement. ⚠ AMBIGUOUS KEY: this run-directory name occurs under more than one campaign (lumi/sbatch/subloss_tgate_modes.sbatch, lumi/sbatch/subspace_loss_grid.sbatch); the variants above are the candidates and are usually the same experiment ported between containers. Disambiguate by the parent directory before relying on one.
lreq_goa_lr1e4.purpose_evidence: lumi/sbatch/subloss_tgate_modes.sbatch + lumi/sbatch/subspace_loss_grid.sbatch headers (Tier-1, ambiguous leaf key)

adamw.purpose: SWEEP-1 of the 8-arm melody control-head sweep (CONTINUITY 2026-08-12, Kim-greenlit): the CONFIG-READY arms only. Varies the first-order levers drivable with existing flags — injection site (--adapter-layers), optimizer (Fusion vs AdamW; Fusion was sovereign for onset density), capacity (dora-rank), target (melody_contour vs hpcp-attribute), and CFG/melody dropout. Base recipe = the proven headb_melody, moved onto FusionOpt. The MORPHOLOGICAL arms (soft-rank/contour loss, k=3 temporal kernel, chroma384) needed code+data that did not exist yet and were deferred to SWEEP-2.

wfleet_avp_t1024_a45_fp32_s1.purpose: B7 MIR-timeseries conditioner bracket (CONTINUITY 2026-08-21, Kim direct: "train some really traditional models, using our mir data as conditioners, probably rank 32 DoRAs... target is every feature we have... goa+avp aug mixed set"). Each arm = medium-base + DoRA-rows r32 + a zero-init per-frame additive control projection on the DiT's native modular local-cond inlet (blocks 12-23 = W's layer-map union), fed REAL MIR curves from the target crop, teacher-forced, per-item control dropout 0.2 as the CFG null. The PACK knob selects the feature family; 'all' = 36 channels (band-RMS 4, stem RMS/onset 8, rhythm 3, HPCP 12, spectral 4, position 1, f0 4 goa-only).

x0eq_goa.purpose: E1a, the x0-EQUIVALENT LOSS arms (CONTINUITY 2026-07-31, Kim "go on with the tests"). JLT port (arXiv 2605.27102): sigma^2-weighted v-loss == x0-space MSE for a v-output head, removing the isotropic covariance floor that swamps low-variance eigendirections. The mechanism was MEASURED live before the run — the v-trained base recovers low-lambda eigendirections 2-8x worse per unit signal, worst at sigma 0.2. Arms: --x0-equiv-loss alone (the parameterization lever solo), and combined with subspace K=5. Recipe = lreq_goa_lr1e4 exactly, so the three melody-wall attacks compare on one axis system.

shuffled.purpose: CONTINUITY 2026-08-17, Kim direct: "stage yet one more fp32 full-ft comparison at t512: lr 3e-5 and 1e-4 (I have a feeling Fusion goes fast, I want to see about a bit slower rates if it finds some smaller paths to new places), EMA, batch of 2, GAS 2... Datasets: suomisoundi, goa large, avp aug x8 ... #1 hyperball, #2 EDM2, #3 both." Six arms = 3 MODES x 2 LRs, testing whether bounding the fine-tune's DESTINATION (unlike warmup/EMA/AdaGC, which bound the path) prevents the drone/latent-scale runaway. hyperball = whole-tensor ‖W‖_F frozen at ‖W0‖_F optimizer-side on every spectral matrix; edm2 = per-output-channel direction normalised with a learnable per-channel gain on the output projection only (weaker, more expressive); both = hyperball on the bulk + gain control at the output. Both retrofit-safe (reproduce the pretrained function at step 0). ⚠ Hyperball (arXiv 2606.16899, Wen/Dang/Lyu/Ma/Liang) fixes norms to HYPERPARAMETER-DERIVED CONSTANTS, not to init — freezing at ‖W0‖_F is OUR choice, not the paper's.

lreq_goa_lr2e4.purpose: LR x epoch x weight EQUIVALENCE GRID (CONTINUITY 2026-07-30, Kim greenlit via W; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-lr-steps-weight-equivalence-grid.md). Question: are inference-weight / LR / steps interchangeable along a cumulative-learning axis? The param-space half was already done (‖dW‖ proportional to LR — magnitude invariant; direction cos 0.17-0.47 — flavour diverges). This run supplies the missing pieces: the DIRECTION-MATURITY curve, which needs intermediate checkpoints the adamw sweep never saved, plus the perceptual grid of matched-cumulative triples and weight-for-steps substitution. || The multitorch migration of lr_equiv_grid (CONTINUITY 2026-08-03), moved off sa3.sif because its ROCm 6.2 MIOpen gfx90a find-fallback HANGS. Same experiment as lr_equiv_grid. NOTE arm 1 (lr1e-4) is the shared K=1 BASELINE for the whole melody-wall campaign (subspace / x0-equiv / combined) — do not treat it as a standalone arm. ⚠ AMBIGUOUS KEY: this run-directory name occurs under more than one campaign (lumi/sbatch/lr_equiv_grid.sbatch, lumi/sbatch/lr_equiv_grid_mt.sbatch); the variants above are the candidates and are usually the same experiment ported between containers. Flagship arms take the top-CLAP recipe levers (alpha<rank "adj", augmentation, fp32) on the FULL corpus, plus ablations that isolate each lever from the 320-crop small-set confound Kim caught. rank 128, lr 1e-4, FusionOpt, medium-base, 20 epochs.

fullft_avp_t1024_bf16_lr25e6_sub12v3sel_.purpose: A13. Kim direct 2026-08-22 ~03:00, "let one run roll on alone": AVP, T1024, lr 2.5e-5, FULL-FT, AdamW, subspace-loss weighting in, flat schedule until ep10 then cosine, to ep64. Kim: "This one has a very mellow LR and some nice controls that have been helpful." ⚠ Two things the spec asked for were dropped before writing, deliberately: AdaGC IS NOT IMPLEMENTED anywhere in trainer or optimizer (it exists only as EXPERIMENTS E2, a planned bracket), and spectral WD is FusionOpt-only so it does not apply to an AdamW arm.

fullft_wd_ab_wd0.purpose: REGULARIZATION A/B for the full-FT latent-scale runaway (CONTINUITY 2026-08-10; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-fullft-regularization-ab.md). The first A/B showed plain weight_decay 0.1 BOUNDS the runaway (global std 0.7->5.6 between ep3 and ep7; channels>2.0 went 0->166/256), but wd is BLUNT — it shrinks every weight direction including the subtle feature-bearing ones. This tests gentler, more targeted regularizers: AGC (NFNets scale-relative per-output-unit gradient clip) and an output-std penalty applied in the LOSS rather than the weights, gated to low noise.

subloss_v3sel_k5_tgate.purpose: CONTINUITY 2026-08-15, Kim direct: scale the subspace-weighted RF loss (#59) up from its lightweight DoRA+AdamW grid (K in {2,5,12}, T512) to the full-FT + FusionOpt + EMA + warmup + AGC recipe — on GOA, K=20 (past the old grid's max), T1024, fp32 (Kim: "actually, make it fp32"). ⚠ Flagged at write time as a bigger change than "K12 -> K20": warmup only has meaning under --optimizer fusion, and --use-ema is full-finetune only (LoRA/DoRA force-disable it), so asking for EMA+warmup+AGC necessarily switched off the original K-grid's adapter/optimizer configuration — the arms are NOT a clean continuation of that grid.

e3_metrical.purpose: The metrical-tree positional-encoding experiment, run as a REAL vs SHUFFLED control pair (both arms present: e3_metrical/real and e3_metrical/shuffled). The shuffled arm destroys metrical structure while preserving everything else, so the real-minus-shuffled delta is the whole measurement — read these two together or not at all. ⚠ WEAK: I could not find a doc naming who commissioned it or when; EXPERIMENTS.md's 'E3' is a DIFFERENT item (LatCH head re-validation), so do not resolve the label that way.

fusion_autoscale_lr5e6_control2.note: ATTRIBUTION CONTROL: is the autoscale direction-convergence a property of the optimizer or of the small training set? ANSWER: the optimizer. Different seed (9001) + disjoint 300-track subset reproduced step_cos to 0.5448 vs 0.5390 (delta 0.006) and path_eff 0.880 vs 0.879. BUT the SOUND changed: Kim 'sounds weak, the beat is not steady, like it was trained on more chill stuff, not as engaging'. => weight-space signature is optimizer-driven, timbre is data-driven. Confounded on seed+data+init; a same-data/different-seed arm would separate them. Audiobox rates it HIGHEST (CE 6.92) and is therefore not tracking Kim's judgment on this question.
